paperMakerGuide.title: Printable Paper Maker: Dot Grid, Graph, Lined, Cornell and More
paperMakerGuide.subtitle: Choose a paper style, set the page size, margins and binding space, and download a sharp vector PDF for printing. Up to 50 pages in one file, with no sign-up.
faq: Is the paper maker free, and do I need an account?
It is free and needs no account. The page is built in your browser, so there is nothing to sign up for and no watermark on the result.
What paper styles are included?

Seven: dot grid, graph (square grid), lined, Cornell notes, isometric (dots or lines), music (5-line staff or 6-line guitar TAB) and a monthly habit tracker. Each has its own options, such as spacing, line colour and size.
Will the PDF print sharp?

Yes. Lines, dots and text are vector shapes, not pictures, so they stay crisp at any zoom and on any printer. Print at "Actual size" or 100%, and turn off "Fit to page", so that the spacing is exactly what you chose.
Why do my lines stop short of the edge of the paper?

The tool keeps everything inside your margins so nothing is cut off. Most home printers cannot print right to the edge, and the page warns you if a margin is below about 5 mm. Increase the margin if your printer clips the border.
What does the binding margin do?

It adds 12 mm of extra space on the binding edge, the left side in portrait or the top in landscape, so that hole punches, ring binders and spirals do not cut through the pattern. Switch on the second option to move that space to the opposite side on back pages when you print double-sided.
Can I print many pages at once?
Yes, up to 50 pages in one PDF. If you add page numbers, each page is numbered from the first number you choose. Identical pages are stored once inside the PDF, so even a long bundle stays small.
How do I save my setup for next time?
Press Save settings to download a small file, and Load settings to open it again. Nothing is stored on a server, so keep the file somewhere you can find it.
Does it draw a treble or bass clef?

No. The clef symbol cannot be drawn with the standard PDF fonts, so the music sheet marks a box at the start of each staff for you to draw the clef by hand. The five lines, the barlines and the six-line TAB layout are complete.
Can I use non-English names in the habit tracker?

Names with Latin letters and accents work. Letters from other scripts, such as Hindi, Arabic or Chinese, cannot be shown with the standard PDF font and appear as a question mark. You can leave the names blank and write them by hand.
How do I print a whole bundle?
Press Download PDF, open the file and print it with "Actual size" selected. The Print this sheet button prints only the sheet shown in the preview.
Can I make hexagon, calligraphy, cross-stitch or storyboard paper?
Yes. Hexagon grid, Calligraphy, Cross-stitch chart and Storyboard are in the Paper style list, each with its own size and layout options.
Can I share my settings with someone?
Yes. Press "Copy link to these settings". The link reopens the same sheet. The settings are stored after the # sign in the address, so they are not sent to any server.
Can I add punch-hole guides or print two A5 pages on an A4 sheet?
Yes. The Extras section has 2, 3 and 4 hole guides at standard spacing, a corner label, and a two-up layout that puts two A5 pages on one A4 sheet with a dashed cut line.
Is my information uploaded or stored?

No. The sheet is drawn and the PDF is built in your browser, and nothing is sent to {{siteName}}. The page still loads advertising and other resources from the network. Saved settings are a small file that you download yourself.

dotGridGuide.title: Dot Grid Paper Generator: Free Printable Bullet Journal Paper
dotGridGuide.subtitle: Make printable dot grid paper for bullet journals, sketching and lettering. Choose 3.5, 5 or 7 mm spacing, the dot size, the page and the binding margin, then download a vector PDF.
faq: What is dot grid paper used for?
It is popular for bullet journals, planners, sketching, lettering, diagrams and note taking. The dots give you structure for straight lines and equal spacing without the heavy look of a full grid.
What dot spacing should I choose?
5 mm is the usual choice for journals and notes. 3.5 mm packs more in and suits small handwriting or A5 pages. 7 mm gives room for large writing, drawing and layouts.
Which page size is best for a bullet journal?
A5 is the most common journal size and fits easily in a bag. A4 suits planners and big spreads, and US Letter is the standard in North America. All are available.
Why does the grid look centered?
The tool fits whole cells inside your margins and centers them, so the left and right edges look even and no dot is cut off at the margin.
How do I print it without scaling?
In the print window choose "Actual size" or 100% and turn off "Fit to page" or "Scale to fit". Otherwise the printer may shrink the page and change the spacing.
Can I make a whole notebook?
Yes. Set the number of pages up to 50, print them double-sided and bind them. Switch on the binding margin and the double-sided option so that the holes do not cut through the dots.
Does it work for left-handed writers?
Yes. You can move the binding space by choosing which margins to enlarge, and a spiral or a loose binder suits both hands. The grid itself is symmetrical.
Is my information uploaded or stored?

No. The sheet is drawn and the PDF is built in your browser, and nothing is sent to {{siteName}}. The page still loads advertising and other resources from the network. Saved settings are a small file that you download yourself.

graphPaperGuide.title: Graph Paper Generator: Free Printable Grid Paper
graphPaperGuide.subtitle: Make printable graph paper with squares of 2.5, 5 or 10 mm, darker lines every fifth or tenth line, optional x and y axes and a light colour to save ink. Download a vector PDF.
faq: What size squares should I use?

5 mm is the standard for school maths and general notes. 10 mm is good for large graphs, early learners and posters. 2.5 mm is for detailed engineering sketches, circuit layouts and anything that needs fine resolution.
Why would I want darker lines every fifth or tenth line?

They make counting squares and reading values off a graph much faster. With 5 mm squares and a darker line every fifth line, each large square is 25 mm; with every tenth line it is 50 mm, which suits centimetre-based work.
What do the axes option do?
It draws a darker horizontal and vertical line through the middle of the grid, so you can plot points with positive and negative values straight away. Turn it off for blank squared paper.
Is this graph paper metric or imperial?
The spacing is in millimetres. For an imperial feel, use about 6.35 mm for quarter-inch squares or 2.54 mm for tenth-inch squares by moving the slider. The page sizes include US Letter and Legal.
Does the grid fit the page exactly?

The tool fits whole squares inside your margins and centers them, so the grid has even borders and no half squares at the edge. If you need the grid to reach the margins exactly, choose a square size that divides the printable width.
What colour is best for graph paper?

A light blue or gray is the traditional choice, since your pencil or pen stands out. Charcoal black prints stronger and suits photocopying or scanning. Pick the lightest tone that stays visible on your printer.
Can I use it for isometric or polar graphs?
This page makes square grids. For isometric grids open the full Printable Paper Maker, which also makes isometric dots and lines.
Is my information uploaded or stored?

No. The sheet is drawn and the PDF is built in your browser, and nothing is sent to {{siteName}}. The page still loads advertising and other resources from the network. Saved settings are a small file that you download yourself.

cornellGuide.title: Cornell Notes Template: Free Printable Note-Taking Paper
cornellGuide.subtitle: Make a printable Cornell notes template with topic, date and subject lines, a cue column, a notes area and a summary box. Adjust the column, the notes style and the page, then download a PDF.
faq: What is the Cornell note-taking method?

It is a way of organising notes developed at Cornell University. You take notes in the wide right column during a lecture or meeting, write questions and key words in the left cue column afterwards, and write a short summary at the bottom. It helps you review and remember.
How do I use the cue column?
After the lecture, read your notes and write questions, keywords or prompts in the left column. When you revise, cover the right side and try to answer the cues from memory.
What goes in the summary box?

Write two or three sentences in your own words that capture the main idea of the page. Doing this soon after class helps you understand the material, and the summary lets you find a page quickly later.
What is the best width for the cue column?
About a quarter to a third of the page works for most people. The default is 28 percent. Make it wider if you write long cues or questions, and narrower if you want more room for notes.
Should the notes area be lined, dotted or plain?
Lined suits written notes, dot grid suits diagrams and mixed notes, and plain suits people who write loosely or draw a lot. You can switch between them and see the result at once.
Can I use the template for meetings and reading?
Yes. The method works for any situation where you take notes and review later, including meetings, textbooks, online courses and interviews.
Can I print it on A5 for a small notebook?
Yes. Choose A5 and add a binding margin if you will punch holes. Reduce the summary height on small pages so there is enough room for notes.

hexPaperGuide.title: Hexagon Graph Paper Generator: Printable Hex Grid for Maps, Games and Chemistry
hexPaperGuide.subtitle: Choose the hexagon size and orientation, add centre dots if you like, and download a clean A4, A5 or Letter PDF. Free, with no sign-up and no watermark.
faq: Is the hexagon grid generator free?
Yes. It is free, needs no account and adds no watermark. The grid is drawn in your browser.
What does the hexagon radius mean?
It is the distance from the centre of a hexagon to any corner, which is also the length of each side. The width across two flat sides is about 1.73 times the radius.
What is the difference between pointy-top and flat-top?

Pointy-top hexagons have a corner at the top and form straight horizontal rows. Flat-top hexagons have a flat edge at the top and form straight vertical columns. Games and map tools use both, so choose the one your rules or software expect.
How do I make 1 inch hexes?
A hexagon 1 inch (25.4 mm) across its flat sides has a radius of about 14.7 mm. Set 14.5 or 15 mm for a close match.
Why are some hexagons missing at the edge?
Only whole hexagons are drawn, so the grid is centred inside your margins and nothing is cut off. Reduce the margins or the radius to fit more.
Can I use it for organic chemistry?
Yes. A small hexagon grid gives rings of even size for drawing benzene and other ring structures. Use a light tone and a 4 to 6 mm radius.
Does the PDF print at the right size?
Yes, if you print at "Actual size" or 100% with "Fit to page" turned off. Print one sheet and measure a hexagon with a ruler to check.

calligraphyGuide.title: Calligraphy Practice Sheet Generator: Slant Guides, x-Height and Ascender Lines
calligraphyGuide.subtitle: Choose a slant angle, the x-height and the ascender and descender depth, and print practice sheets for Copperplate, Spencerian, italic and modern lettering. Free, no sign-up.
faq: Is the calligraphy sheet generator free?
Yes. It is free, needs no account and adds no watermark. The sheet is drawn in your browser.
What slant angle should I use?

Copperplate is commonly taught at about 55 degrees from the baseline, and Spencerian at about 52 degrees. Italic hands are often close to upright, around 5 to 10 degrees from vertical, which is 80 to 85 degrees on this slider.
How is the angle measured?
From the baseline, so a larger number means more upright. 90 degrees gives vertical lines and 55 degrees gives the classic Copperplate lean.
What are the lines on the sheet?
Each group has a heavy baseline, a waist line at the top of small letters, a dashed ascender line above and a dashed descender line below. The slant lines run across all groups.
How do I choose the x-height?
For broad-edge pens, many teachers use about five nib widths. For pointed pens, 4 to 6 mm suits beginners. Larger sizes help when you are learning the shapes.
Can I print a bundle of pages?
Yes, up to 50 pages in one PDF. The identical pages are stored once, so the file stays small.
Why do my lines look pale?
Pale lines are deliberate so your ink stands out. Choose a darker tone or a bold line weight if you want stronger guides, or print on a light-table-friendly paper.

crossStitchGuide.title: Cross-Stitch Pattern Grid Generator: Printable Stitch Chart and Pixel Grid
crossStitchGuide.subtitle: Pick the fabric count, and print a stitch grid with a bold line every 10 squares and centre marks. Also good for pixel art, bead patterns and mosaic designs. Free, no sign-up.
faq: Is the cross-stitch grid generator free?
Yes. It is free, needs no account and adds no watermark.
What is a fabric count?
The number of stitches per inch. 14-count Aida has 14 stitches in each inch, so each square on the chart is 1.81 mm. Higher counts give smaller stitches and finer detail.
How big will my finished piece be?
Divide the number of stitches by the count. A design 140 stitches wide on 14-count fabric is 10 inches wide, which is about 25.4 cm.
Why is there a darker line every 10 squares?
Counting is the slowest part of charting. Marking every 10th line lets you count in tens and place stitches accurately without losing your place.
What are the dashed centre lines for?
Starting from the middle of the chart and the middle of the fabric keeps the design centred. The dashed lines show where to begin.
Can I use it for pixel art and beads?
Yes. Each square is one pixel, stitch or bead. For 5 mm beads, use the Beads 5 mm option. For pixel art, a larger square gives you more room to colour.
Does the grid cover the whole page?
It fits as many whole squares as the margins allow and centres them. Reduce the margins or choose a higher count to get a bigger chart.

sections.heading: What the Printable Paper Maker does
paragraphs: It lets you design the exact paper you need and print it at home or at a print shop. Instead of searching for a template that is almost right, you choose the style, the spacing, the page size and the margins, see the result at once and download a PDF.

The preview is drawn from the same shapes that go into the PDF, so what you see is what prints. There is no sign-up, no watermark and no upload, which makes it quick to make a single page or a whole notebook.

sections.heading: Seven paper styles for real uses
paragraphs: Dot grid suits bullet journals and sketching, with spacing from 3.5 mm to 7 mm. Graph paper suits maths and engineering, with 2.5, 5 or 10 mm squares and darker lines every fifth or tenth line. Lined paper comes in narrow, college and wide spacing, with an optional margin line and a dotted midline for handwriting practice.

Cornell notes gives you a topic, date and subject block, a cue column, a notes area and a summary box. Isometric paper helps with 3D sketching, in dots or lines. Music paper offers five-line staves or six-line guitar TAB, and the habit tracker gives you a month of boxes to tick.

sections.heading: Margins, binding and double-sided printing
paragraphs: Notebooks and binders need space for holes. Switch on the binding margin and the tool adds 12 mm on the binding edge so that nothing is punched through. For double-sided printing, the second option moves the space to the other edge on the back of each sheet, so the holes line up when the pages are turned.
Your margins stay inside the printable area of the page. If a margin is smaller than about 5 mm, the page warns you, because many home printers cannot print that close to the edge.

sections.heading: Saving ink and keeping lines readable
paragraphs: Heavy dark grids compete with your writing and use a lot of ink. The tone presets (soft gray, slate blue, muted sepia, blueprint cyan and charcoal) and the line weight choices let you make the pattern as light as you like. Soft gray at normal weight works for most note taking.
If you print on a laser printer, thin lines in light tones may look faint, so try the Normal or Bold weight. Test one page before you print a whole bundle.

sections.heading: Bundles, headers and saved settings
paragraphs: Choose how many pages you want, from one to fifty. Add a header bar with date, subject, project or page number fields, and the pages are numbered from the starting number you pick. This is how you turn a sheet into a ready-to-use notebook or a binder refill.
Save your settings to a file when you have a setup you like, and load it again next time. The file holds only your choices, such as the style and the spacing, and never your writing.

sections.heading: What is dot grid paper?
paragraphs: Dot grid paper is a page covered in a regular pattern of small dots. Because the dots are small, they disappear behind your writing yet still give you points to line up against. You can write, draw boxes, make tables, sketch charts and lay out a page without a ruler.
It became popular with bullet journal users, who plan their weeks and months in a custom layout, and with designers, who use it for quick sketches and lettering practice.

sections.heading: Choosing the right spacing
paragraphs: The spacing is the distance between dots. A 5 mm grid is the most common because it suits normal handwriting and lets you draw a neat box in a few squares. A 3.5 mm grid is denser, good for small notes, tiny checklists and A5 pages. A 7 mm grid is open, which suits bigger handwriting, drawing and children.
You can also set any spacing from 2 to 15 mm with the slider. If your pen has a thick nib, use a wider grid so the dots do not get lost under the ink.

sections.heading: Dot size and colour
paragraphs: Fine dots are the lightest and best for detailed work, medium dots are a balanced default, and bold dots are easy to see when you work fast or print on a rough paper. Soft gray keeps the grid in the background. Slate blue, sepia and cyan add a little colour, and charcoal black gives the strongest dots.
Print a test page first. Every printer and every paper shows dots a little differently, and a quick test saves time and ink.

sections.heading: From one page to a notebook
paragraphs: Pick your page size and margins, then set the number of pages. Switch on the binding margin to leave 12 mm for punched holes or spiral rings, and turn on the double-sided option if you print both sides, which puts the extra space on the correct edge of the back pages.
You can fold, cut and bind the sheets yourself, take the PDF to a print shop for a spiral bound book, or put the pages in a ring binder.

sections.heading: Printing tips
paragraphs: Use Actual size or 100% scale. Choose the paper type that matches your sheet, and a standard or draft quality setting is enough for light dots. If dots appear at slightly different spacing than you chose, check that your printer is not scaling the page.
The PDF is made of vector shapes, so the dots stay round and sharp however you zoom in. Nothing is uploaded.

sections.heading: What graph paper is for
paragraphs: Graph paper is paper printed with a grid of equal squares. Students use it to plot functions and data, engineers use it for scale drawings and layouts, designers use it for pixel art, floor plans and wireframes, and knitters and cross-stitchers use it for patterns. The squares keep lines straight and proportions even.
Buying the exact size you need can be hard, and printing your own is cheap. This generator lets you choose the squares, the page and the lines to suit the job.

sections.heading: Choosing the square size
paragraphs: Square size decides how much detail you can show. 2.5 mm squares give 40 squares per 100 mm, which is fine for detailed technical drawings. 5 mm squares are the school standard and suit most graphs. 10 mm squares make large, clear plots and are easy for young children to use.
Use the slider for anything in between, such as 6.35 mm for a quarter inch. The page shows the size in millimetres so there is no conversion to do.

sections.heading: Major lines, axes and counting
paragraphs: Every fifth or tenth line can be made darker. This works like the heavier lines on a ruler: your eye groups the squares in fives or tens, so you can count and read values faster. Combined with the optional axes through the centre, you get paper that is ready for plotting.
Use the axes for coordinate geometry, physics graphs and data plots. Leave them off when you want a plain grid for drawing, planning or pattern design.

sections.heading: Page sizes, margins and colour
paragraphs: Choose A4 for general work, A5 for a small notebook, US Letter or Legal for North American paper sizes, and landscape for wide graphs. Margins stay clear of the edge of the page, so no square is cut off when your printer cannot print to the edge.
A light slate blue or cyan is easy to read and saves ink. If you need to scan or photocopy the graph, charcoal black gives more contrast.

sections.heading: Printing and using the result
paragraphs: Print at Actual size or 100% so the squares are the size you chose, then check one square against a ruler. The PDF is vector, so the lines stay sharp in print and on screen. Nothing is uploaded, and you can print as many pages as you want, up to fifty in one file.
If you plan to draw on the paper with a pencil, a light line weight keeps the grid from competing with your work. For pen drawings, use Normal.

sections.heading: What a Cornell notes page looks like
paragraphs: A Cornell page is divided into four areas. At the top are lines for the topic, the date and the subject. Down the left is a narrow cue column, on the right a wide notes area, and across the bottom a summary box. The layout turns note taking into a study system and not only a record.
This generator draws the page for you, with labels so that you remember what each area is for. You can change the widths and the style of the notes area to suit how you work.

sections.heading: How to use it in class or in a meeting
paragraphs: During the session, write your notes in the right-hand column. Use short phrases, not full sentences, and leave space between ideas. Do not worry about the cue column yet.

Soon after, read the notes, fill the cue column with questions or keywords for each section, and write a summary at the bottom of the page. These two steps are the most important, because they make you process what you wrote.

sections.heading: Reviewing with the cue column
paragraphs: To revise, cover the notes column and read the cues. Try to answer each from memory, then slide the cover back to check. This gives you active recall, which is a more effective way to learn than rereading.
Review within a day, then again after a week and before the exam. The summary lets you scan many pages quickly to find what you need.

sections.heading: Setting up the template
paragraphs: Adjust the width of the cue column from 15 to 40 percent, and the height of the summary box. Choose lined, dot grid or plain for the notes. Add a binding margin for a binder or a spiral, and a page number when you take notes across many sheets.
Pick a light tone so the structure is visible but does not compete with your handwriting. Soft gray and slate blue work well.

sections.heading: Printing a stack of pages
paragraphs: Set the number of pages and download the PDF. For a semester, print a few dozen and keep them in a binder with a divider for each subject. Print at Actual size, and use double-sided printing with the binding option for a tidy result.
Everything is made in your browser. Your settings are not stored on a server, and you can save them in a small file to use again next term.

sections.heading: What the Hexagon Graph Paper Generator does
paragraphs: It draws a grid of regular hexagons on a page and gives you a PDF to print. You choose the size of the hexagons, whether they point up or lie flat, the page size, the margins, the ink tone and the line weight. There is no fixed template to put up with: a small grid for chemistry sketches and a large grid for a campaign map are both a few clicks.
The page is built in your browser as vector lines, so the grid stays sharp at any print size and the file is small. Nothing you set is uploaded.

sections.heading: Pointy top or flat top
paragraphs: A regular hexagon can sit on a corner or on an edge. With a corner at the top, the hexagons line up in horizontal rows and every second row is shifted sideways by half a hexagon. With a flat edge at the top, they line up in vertical columns and every second column is shifted up by half a hexagon.

The choice matters for games and software. Many tabletop games use pointy-top maps for rows of terrain, while other rules and programs assume flat-top. If you are copying a map into another tool, check which one it uses and match it, otherwise coordinates will not line up.

sections.heading: Choosing the size
paragraphs: Size is set by the radius, the distance from the centre to a corner. Because the hexagon is regular, this is also the length of one side. The distance between the centres of two neighbouring hexagons is about 1.73 times the radius, which is useful when a rule says each hexagon is a fixed distance, such as one mile or one move.

For miniatures, work back from the figure: a base about 25 mm wide fits a hexagon of roughly 14.5 mm radius. For notes, doodles and patchwork templates, 4 to 8 mm is comfortable. Use the quick buttons for common sizes, then fine-tune with the slider.

sections.heading: Uses for hexagon paper
paragraphs: Hexagon grids are used for role-playing and war-game maps, board game design, strategy planning, tile-laying puzzles, mosaic and honeycomb art, patchwork and quilting layouts, and the rings of organic chemistry. Designers use them to plan layouts where each cell has six equal neighbours, which a square grid cannot give.
Turn on the centre dots if you will place tokens or count steps from cell to cell. The dots mark the exact middle of each hexagon and do not change the size of the grid.

sections.heading: Printing and fit
paragraphs: The grid is centred inside the margins and only whole hexagons are drawn, so the edge of the pattern is clean. A4, A5, US Letter and US Legal are available in portrait or landscape. If you are printing a map to be cut or joined, leave generous margins and print on the paper size your printer handles best.

Print at 100% scale with fit-to-page off, then check one hexagon with a ruler. Many printers also leave a thin unprintable border, so keep margins of at least 5 mm. A lighter ink tone makes the grid easy to draw over and saves ink.

sections.heading: Combining with other options
paragraphs: Add punch-hole guides and a binding margin to make pages for a binder. Use the corner label for a campaign name, a class or the word Draft. Choose a bundle of up to 50 pages to print a whole notebook in one go, and use the link button to share the exact settings with a group.
If you need a square grid, a dot grid or an isometric grid instead, they are in the same tool, and the settings you pick for page, margins and tone carry over.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: The generator draws regular hexagons only, and it does not number or label the cells. Draw coordinates by hand, or add them in a design program. Very small hexagons on a low-quality printer may look heavy, so test one page before you print a bundle.
Everything happens in your browser, and nothing you set is stored on a server.

sections.heading: What the Calligraphy Practice Sheet Generator does
paragraphs: It makes guide sheets for lettering practice: horizontal lines that mark the height of small and tall letters, and slanted lines that keep your strokes at a steady angle. You set the angle, the letter height and the spacing, and download a PDF to print as many times as you like.
Most free sheets online are fixed images for one hand and one nib size. Here every measure is adjustable, so the sheet can match the pen you actually use.

sections.heading: The lines on the sheet
paragraphs: Every writing group has four horizontal lines. The baseline is the heavy line the letters sit on. The waist line is the top of lower-case letters such as a, c and e, so the space between waist line and baseline is the x-height. The ascender line is the top of tall letters such as b, d and l. The descender line is the bottom of letters such as g, p and y.

The ascender and descender distances are set as multiples of the x-height. The defaults are a starting point, since the proportions vary between scripts and teachers. Change them to match the exemplar you are copying.

sections.heading: Slant angle
paragraphs: Slant is the lean of the downstrokes. In Copperplate, practice sheets commonly use 55 degrees from the baseline, and Spencerian is commonly taught at about 52. Upright hands such as many italic and modern brush styles use a small lean or none. The quick buttons set the common angles, and the slider covers everything in between.
The slant lines keep your downstrokes parallel, which does more for neat lettering than almost anything else. If your letters drift, slow down and check each stroke against the nearest guide line.

sections.heading: Choosing a size
paragraphs: Large letters show the shapes and are easier to control while you learn. Small letters train fine control but magnify mistakes. A common approach is to start with an x-height of about 5 to 6 mm and reduce it as your hand steadies.

For broad-edge pens, work from the nib: many italic and gothic exercises are sized in nib widths, with an x-height of about five widths. Measure your nib by drawing a row of squares, then convert to millimetres and enter it.

sections.heading: Paper, ink and tone
paragraphs: Calligraphy ink often bleeds on thin paper, so print the guides on smooth, heavy paper or print them and place them under a lightweight sheet on a light box. A light tone such as soft gray or slate blue keeps the lines visible without competing with your ink.
If the guide lines show through your final piece, switch to the ultra-fine weight and the lightest tone, or use the guide as an underlay rather than writing directly on it.

sections.heading: Practice routine
paragraphs: Begin each session with warm-up strokes: straight downstrokes along the slant, ovals and compound curves. Then move to single letters, joined groups and finally words. Short, regular sessions of 20 minutes work better than a long weekly session.
Use the page bundle option to make a stack of identical sheets, add your name with the corner label, and number the pages so you can see progress over time.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: The sheets provide guides only. They do not contain letter exemplars or alphabets, which depend on the style you are learning, so keep an exemplar beside you. Angles are drawn exactly, but printers can stretch a page slightly, so print at 100% scale.
The tool runs in your browser, and nothing you set is uploaded.

sections.heading: What the Cross-Stitch Pattern Grid Generator does
paragraphs: It prints a grid of squares where each square stands for one stitch. You choose the fabric count and the tool works out the exact square size, then draws a bold line every 10 squares and dashed centre lines. You can colour the squares by hand with pencils, markers or symbols to design your own pattern.
The grid is drawn in your browser as sharp vector lines, so it prints cleanly at any size, and the settings are not uploaded.

sections.heading: Fabric count and square size
paragraphs: Aida fabric is sold by count, the number of stitches per inch. A square on the chart matches one stitch, so the grid has to match your fabric to predict the size. The tool converts the count into millimetres: 11 count is 2.31 mm per square, 14 count is 1.81 mm, 16 count is 1.59 mm and 18 count is 1.41 mm.

Small squares fit more stitches on a page but are harder to colour. For design work, many people chart on a larger grid than the fabric count and rely on the count only when working out the finished size.

sections.heading: Working out the finished size
paragraphs: Divide the stitches by the count. A 100 by 150 stitch design on 14 count measures about 7.1 by 10.7 inches, which is about 18 by 27 cm. On 18 count the same design is smaller, about 5.6 by 8.3 inches.

Remember to leave extra fabric around the design for framing, usually at least 2 inches on each side. Choosing the count before you design avoids a pattern that is too big or too small once it is stitched.

sections.heading: Counting made easier
paragraphs: The darker line every 10 squares works as a ruler. When you transfer a design from the chart to the fabric, count the tens first and then the squares inside them. Mark every 10th row and column on the fabric with a water-soluble pen if it helps.

Start from the centre. The dashed centre lines show the middle of the chart. Fold your fabric in quarters to find its centre and match the two before the first stitch, so the design lands in the middle of the fabric.

sections.heading: Beyond cross-stitch
paragraphs: The same grid suits pixel art, bead and brick patterns, mosaic and tile planning, knitting and crochet charts when the stitch proportions are close to square, and even simple map drawing. The Beads 5 mm setting makes each square about the size of a standard bead.
For colour, use pencils or fine markers and a key of symbols or numbers beside the grid. Print a few pages and keep one clean copy for the final chart.

sections.heading: Printing tips
paragraphs: Print at 100% scale, with fit-to-page turned off, if you want the squares to match real stitches. Measure ten squares with a ruler to check. A light tone lets your colours stand out, and a darker tone is better if you plan to photocopy the chart.
Add a corner label with your project name and use the page bundle to print several sheets for a large chart that you tape together.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: The tool does not convert pictures into patterns and does not assign thread colours. It gives you an accurate, printable grid to design on. Printers may stretch a page slightly, so charts meant to join across sheets should be printed on the same printer in one session.
Everything runs in your browser, and nothing you set is sent to a server.
